subject: Streamline Retail renewal + capacity uplift – updated term sheet
messages:
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@streamline-retail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Hsu <danielle@streamline-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift proposal

Hi Priyom —

Per our renewal window next month, Danielle and I put together a proposal that would lock our pricing for the first 6 months, and add a capacity uplift so we can roll out new features H2. High-level:

- Term: 12 months starting 2027-04-01
- Commit: 2.5x current committed tokens (spike-friendly burst pool)
- Price: hold current unit price for first 6 months, then revert to list + 8% uplift thereafter
- Credit ask: $200k one-time credit applied across the first 4 invoices (amortized)

Attached is the term sheet (Streamline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf). We need an answer by 2027-02-18 to align with procurement cycles.

Alyssa
Alyssa Green
Head of Platform, Streamline Retail
alyssa@streamline-retail.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@streamline-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift proposal

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear proposal and the term sheet. We're excited about the expanded scope — Streamline has been a great partner. A few quick clarifying questions so we can put a clean counter together for procurement:

1) The 2.5x uplift — is that in committed tokens/month or total committed usage over the year?
2) Can you confirm whether the amortized credit needs to appear as a line-item credit or applied as invoice-level dollar offsets?
3) Does Streamline require IP/data segregation above standard Dedicated controls (we have a Private option but that changes lead times)?

Initial thoughts from my side:
- We can do a 6-month price hold if commit increases by at least 30% (we need the uplift to justify the hold).
- For credits, we prefer a one-time credit rather than amortized credits (simpler for both finance teams) — suggest $75k one-time onboarding credit if we agree to a 30% commit uplift.
- I'll loop in Ben on finance to confirm break-even math and Marissa on post-sale support capacity.

Can you confirm the exact uplift metric and your preferred billing treatment for the credit? If you can get back by EOD 2/15 we should be able to finalize a doc and send to procurement the following week.

Thanks,

Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Streamline proposal — internal ask

Folks — forwarding Streamline's ask. TL;DR: they want 6-month price hold + $200k amortized credit if we agree to a 2.5x commit. Procurement wants clear invoicing structure. My quick margin check: at 2.5x commit a 6-month hold with $200k amortization is tight on margin for us given their usage profile.

Proposal I think is reasonable to put on the table:
- Offer: 12-month term, commit increase of 30% (not necessarily full 2.5x)
- Concession: 6-month price hold at current rate if they commit to 30% uplift
- Credit: $75,000 one-time invoice credit (applied to first invoice)
- Other: include a 90-day SLA ramp clause and P0/P1 support hours allocation (Marissa to confirm)

If finance can accept $75k, we keep good margin and give Streamline meaningful onboarding $$ and a 6-month certainty window. Ben — do you see any red flags with the $75k and a 30% uplift? Also legal will need to weigh in on the price hold language (term start / rollback mechanics).

Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Updated term sheet and counter for Streamline renewal

Hi Alyssa and Danielle —

Thanks for the proposal and for the patience while we reviewed internally. We want to keep Streamline's rollouts on schedule and be a helpful partner on pricing. Based on internal alignment, here's our counter-proposal:

- Term: 12 months starting 2027-04-01
- Commit: 1.3x current committed tokens (monthly committed baseline) — this preserves flexibility while delivering guaranteed capacity
- Price hold: Redwood will lock current unit pricing for the first 6 months of the term
- Credit: $75,000 one-time invoice credit applied to the first invoice (Streamline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf attached)
- SLA/support: 90-day ramp plan + defined P0/P1 support hours included for the first 3 months (Marissa will coordinate kickoff)

If this works for Streamline we'll prepare the updated term sheet for signature (DocuSign link below) and aim to have countersigned docs by 2027-02-24 to hit your procurement window.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc-Streamline-Renewal
Attachment: Streamline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Please let me know if you'd like a quick 20-min call to walk the changes.

Best,
